findings: Barbot's proof (compactness of the symmetric maps of norm <= 1 and the forms Q(lambda, v), l.3040-3099) can be replaced by one argument: if c|Tu|^2 <= <u|Tu> on E (c > 0), then T^(e + w) = T e for e in E, w orthogonal to T(E), is well defined (E cap T(E)^perp lies in ker T), defined everywhere (E + T(E)^perp = V), symmetric and satisfies the same inequality; the case y- = -y+ reduces to it through P = (1 + y+ T)/2, since |P u|^2 <= <u|P u> iff |y+ T u| <= |u|. labels.label: bprop:sanloxo

hypotheses.paper: Gamma without loxodromic element; Benoist's theorem
hypotheses.note: Benoist as the external `BenoistNoLox d` (Flat/Externals); the rest proved through `lorentz_trichotomy`

sorries.obstruction: FALSE AS STATED for d >= 5 (closer, 2026-11-01). Counterexample (Minkowski 5, Barbot's coordinates nolToMink, P0bar = R^4 = H the quaternions): Gamma generated by the LINEAR isometries with NolParams (L_a, 0, 0, 0, 0) and (L_b, 0, e, 0, 0), L_q z = q z, a, b a free pair of unit quaternions (e.g. (1+2i)/sqrt5, (1+2j)/sqrt5, free by unique factorisation of Lipschitz quaternions of norm 5^n; or any free pair in SU(2)), e != 0. (i) L(Gamma) fixes v0 = ofNull 1 0 0 and lies in lorentz 5 (det L_q = 1, connected group). (ii) The horosphere action lambda(gamma) = (z -> L_q z + c) defines a homomorphism Gamma -> SU(2), q, which is injective because F_2 -> <a,b> is; so q = 1 forces gamma = 1, and for q != 1 the map L_q - 1 is invertible (H is a division ring), so lambda(gamma) has a fixed point z, the horosphere point over z is a timelike vector fixed by L(gamma), and L(gamma) is IsElliptic (isElliptic_of_fixed_timelike). (iii) A finite-index Gamma' contains gamma_a^k and gamma_b^m (k, m >= 1). A fixed timelike vector X of Gamma' has y(X) != 0 (Q = 2xy + |z|^2 < 0), so after scaling to y = 1 its z-coordinate is a common fixed point of lambda(Gamma'): a^k z = z gives z = 0 (a^k != 1), while lambda(gamma_b^m) 0 = (1 + L_b + ... + L_b^(m-1)) e = (L_b^m - 1)(L_b - 1)^(-1) e != 0 (b^m != 1). Contradiction. The previous obstruction's 'holds when Gamma is finitely generated (bounded orbits)' is refuted as well (this Gamma is 2-generated; equivalently H^1(F_2, R^4) != 0 and restriction to finite index is injective). True for d <= 3 (P0bar of dimension <= 2: an all-elliptic subgroup of Isom+(R^2) has no nontrivial translation, embeds in SO(2), is abelian, and commuting nontrivial rotations share their centre; d <= 2 trivial) and whenever lambda(Gamma) is discrete (Bieberbach: virtually a translation lattice, all elliptic => finite => fixed point). d = 4 (P0bar = R^3) not settled. A correct statement needs an added hypothesis from the section-8 data (e.g. discreteness of lambda(Gamma), or properness of Gamma on Omega(S~) = M^n, which holds in this branch since all of Gamma is elliptic); that is a statement change for the orchestrator. Downstream: `nonloxodromic` (third branch) and Classification.lean:314 consume this lemma.

findings: l.2621-2622 ('up to finite index, L(Gamma) preserves an isotropic vector v0 and Gamma contains a parabolic element gamma_1') does not follow from Prop 9.1 as stated: 9.1 allows L(Gamma') fixing v0 and consisting of elliptic elements only, a branch §9 never treats (it should reduce to the elliptic case).

Closer 2026-11-01: `exists_timelike_fixed_of_elliptic_of_null` is FALSE as stated for d >= 5 (2-generated counterexample from a free pair of unit quaternions acting on P0bar = H by left multiplication, with a non-coboundary cocycle; see the sorry entry). The paper's Zariski-closure argument (l.2596-2597) does not rescue it: the Zariski closure of lambda(Gamma) is SU(2) x| R^4, whose extra elements are parabolic, not loxodromic, so Benoist does not exclude it. Whether Barbot's actual Gamma (a holonomy group acting properly on Omega(S~) = M^n in this branch) can be of this kind is not settled here.
questions: exists_timelike_fixed_of_elliptic_of_null is false for d >= 5 (counterexample in the sorry entry). Which hypothesis should be added (discreteness of lambda(Gamma); or the section-8 data, properness on Omega(S~) = M^n), and should `nonloxodromic`'s third branch be rerouted through it? Classification.lean:314 also consumes the lemma.

labels.label: [9.E] the elliptic case (prose, l.2604-2617)

hypotheses.paper: L(Gamma) in SO(n-1) up to conjugacy, up to finite index
hypotheses.note: Gamma' <= Gamma of finite index (`Gamma'.relIndex Gamma != 0`, added at the 2026-11-01 audit: without it Gamma' = bot makes the statement false, e.g. for a Misner spacetime) whose linear parts fix a timelike vector; all of Gamma is then elliptic (`isElliptic_of_relIndex`)
the external `BieberbachI` (Flat/Bieberbach) for every dimension <= d + 1

sorries.obstruction: proved: all of Gamma elliptic, Omega(S~) = M^n, Gamma free on M^n (`omegaS_eq_univ_of_relIndex`). Missing: proper discontinuity of Gamma'' on all of M^n (Develop's `holonomy_proper` is on Sigma only; Prop 8.10's properness on Omega(S~) is needed) and the bundled quotient B; the transport of Gamma' to E ≃ᵃⁱ E for the euclidean form fixed by L(Gamma') and the maximal translation subspace U (BieberbachMaxConclusion, mem_direction_of_fixed); RestrictsIn after an index-2 passage; IsTranslationSpacetime for Gamma''_U\U, which needs the span of the translation vectors spacelike — to be derived from (CC') (an invariant graph t = x2 + h with h periodic along a dense line cannot be strictly contracting)

findings: 'quotients of M^n by a group of translations by spacelike translation vectors' (l.588-590) is not 'translations whose span is spacelike' (BARBOT-THEOREMS §1's reading, Examples' IsTranslationSpacetime): in M^4 the translations by e1 and e0 + e2 + sqrt2 e1 generate a rank-2 group all of whose nonzero vectors are spacelike while its span contains the null vector e0 + e2 (`spacelike_translations_null_span`). Its quotient carries no invariant entire acausal graph (an invariant graph f = x2 + h, h doubly periodic, cannot be strictly contracting along e2), so (CC') should exclude it, but [9.E]'s 'translation spacetime' then needs that argument.
questions: Is a translation spacetime (l.588-590) meant with a spacelike span of translation vectors (as BARBOT-THEOREMS §1 reads it), so that the degenerate-span rank-2 groups are excluded by definition?

labels.label: [9.P] the parabolic set-up and coordinates (prose, l.2619-2735)
findings: l.2659: for a linear gamma in A(v0), U(gamma) is the preimage under pi_1 of the complement of a point (u + y v != 0, l.2929), not of 'a half-line'; the component I' is still an interval.

labels.label: rem choixcoord (Rem 9.2, l.2737-2760)
findings: Rem 9.2's changes of vn are not changes of null frame: |vn + w|^2 = |w|^2 for w in P0bar and |vn + a v0|^2 = 2a (`frameChange_null`). The correct change is vn' = vn + w - (|w|^2/2) v0, i.e. the coordinates (x, z, y) -> (x + <w|z> - (y/2)|w|^2, z - y w, y), the action of (id, 0, -w, 0, 0) in A(v0); under it u' = u, v' = v and Barbot's mu' = mu + <u|w> hold exactly (`choixcoord`). The first bullet (w in Delta0) is not a frame change at all.

labels.label: [9.b] triviality of b (prose, l.2767-2787)

hypotheses.note: gamma_1 purely unipotent (R = id); b(gamma_1) = 0 is proved from v(gamma_1) != 0 (`b_eq_zero_model`, the p^4 coefficient -b^2|v|^2/12)

findings: The argument of l.2776-2787 uses Lemma 7.1 (`blem:paranongh`), false as printed for n >= 4 (Flat/AchronalDomains), and Cor 8.3. Neither is needed: invariance under gamma_0^{±1} makes pi_1(S~) unbounded both ways, and the leading term <u + y v | u + y' v> of Prop 9.3 at heights y0 + k b(gamma_0), y0 - k b(gamma_0) is negative for large k (`b_trivial_model`), for a purely unipotent parabolic gamma_1. For gamma_1 = R U with R != id the analogue (leading term on Fix R) is not written. `b_trivial` states it in M^n (normalised frame): if L(Gamma) fixes v0 = ofNull 1 0 0, Gamma preserves a nonempty acausal S~ and contains gamma_1 with R(gamma_1) = id, v(gamma_1) != 0, then every element of Gamma preserves each null hyperplane {y = c}.

kb_proposals: Barbot's null coordinates are a model `ℝ × E × ℝ` with `Q = 2xy + |z|²` (`Flat/Nonloxodromic`'s `nolQ`, `NolParam`), linked to `𝐌ⁿ` by `nolToMink := ofNull`; an element of `Stab(v₀)` is the data `(R, u, v, μ, b)` with an explicit composition law (`NolParam.mul`), and powers/quadratic leading terms are proved by `ext` + `ring` after `norm_add_sq_real`, keeping `‖u + y • v‖²` as an atom.

To extend a partial linear map from a subspace E by zero on a complement, glue with `LinearPMap.sup` and evaluate through `LinearPMap.sup_apply`; `E ⊔ Fᗮ = ⊤` is easiest through `(E ⊔ Fᗮ)ᗮ = Eᗮ ⊓ F = ⊥` (`Submodule.inf_orthogonal`, `orthogonal_orthogonal`, `orthogonal_eq_bot_iff`).
`Σ` is a reserved token in Lean 4 (sigma types): it cannot be a variable name; nor can `y₋` (subscript minus).

A uniform power lands in a finite-index subgroup without normal cores: `Subgroup.pow_mem_of_relIndex_ne_zero_of_dvd hidx ha (fun _ hm hle => Nat.dvd_factorial hm hle)` gives a ^ (H.relIndex K)! ∈ H for every a ∈ K; conjugates are handled by `conj_pow`.
